_instructions: Descriptions, search tags and category suggestions for every game-icons.net icon shipped in assets/game-icons.net/.
game-icons.net does not license its own metadata, so this file is virtualtabletop's own, written from the RENDERED artwork of each icon (the filename was only a hint).
This file is deliberately NOT loaded by the application - assets/fonts/symbols.json is what the icon pickers read. Keep the two in sync.
HOW TO ADD NEW ICONS FROM GAME-ICONS.NET (for a future AI run):
1. Drop the new SVGs into assets/game-icons.net/<artist>/<icon-name>.svg, keeping game-icons.net's own artist folder and file name.
2. Rebuild the sprite sheets, because symbols.json addresses them by index:
raise the resource limits in /etc/ImageMagick-6/policy.xml to 8GiB, then run
montage -background none assets/game-icons.net/*/*.svg -geometry 48x48+0+0 -tile 60x assets/game-icons.net/overview48.png
(and the same with -geometry 24x24+0+0 for overview24.png). The montage order is the shell glob order of */*.svg,
so EVERY icon's index shifts when a name sorts before an existing one - always regenerate all indices, never patch a single entry.
3. LOOK AT EACH NEW ICON as an image - render it, do not guess from the file name - and write, for each one:
- description: one sentence describing what is actually drawn.
- tags: up to 20 lowercase search terms for discoverability (synonyms, uses, materials, themes, related concepts).
A search term matches the BEGINNING OF A WORD of the file name, but only a WHOLE WORD of the tags (a trailing s/es aside),
so tags are read word by word: 'bear' finds a 'bear trap' but not a 'bearing', and typing 'swor' still finds sword.svg.
A tag therefore has to add a word that neither the file name nor an earlier tag of the same icon already carries - 'star'
is pointless next to 'shooting star' or on shooting-star.svg, but 'fire' next to 'bonfire' is not, because no word matches.
Tag the artwork, not what it could be associated with: a razor tagged 'beard' or a compass tagged 'bearing' shows up in a
search for beards and bearings, which is what a user typing them wants - a razor in a search for 'bear' is not. Write fewer
than 20 tags rather than padding with words that fit every icon of the family alike: the search shows the first 100 matches,
name matches first, so a word carried by a whole section buries the icons that are really about it.
Tags are plain lowercase ASCII (no accents, no '&'): they are what a user types into the search box. Use US spelling -
'defense', 'armor', 'color' - because the match never bridges the two.
- categories: 5 broad category suggestions, most specific first, taken from the vocabulary in `categoryVocabulary` below.
- category: the picker category the icon ends up in - the first of its 5 suggestions that maps to a picker category via `categoryMapping`.
4. Add the same icon to assets/fonts/symbols.json under `Game-icons.net - <category>` as [ spriteIndex, ...the tags ],
and refresh the spriteIndex of every other game-icons entry from the new montage order.
5. Keep the picker categories balanced: if one grows far beyond the others or shrinks to a handful of icons, re-map the vocabulary
in `categoryMapping` and re-assign, rather than inventing a one-off category.
tests/game-icons-metadata.test.js checks all of the above - both files covering the same SVGs, the sprite indices being the
glob order, identical tags in both, the category mapping and every tag rule. Run `npm test` after editing either file.
